items.text: The research item already settled three top-level decisions: (a) reconciliation runs as an in-process goroutine ticker (d1=A), (b) anomaly delivery is a webhook POST, not email or dashboard polling (d2=B), and (c) implementation-level details (schema, thresholds, retry policy) belong in this execute item (d3=A). Those decisions are baked into the plan and are not re-asked here.

The existing intro_anomaly_log pattern lives at api/main.go:1009-1020 (schema) and api/stripe_coupon_service.go:585-620 (insert). The Stripe settings storage + redact/reveal admin pattern is in api/payment_settings_service.go and api/payment_settings_handlers.go and is the template for the new alert-config fields.

Acceptance_allow is already set to scenarios/landing-page-business-suite/api/** and scenarios/landing-page-business-suite/docs/**, which fully covers the planned changes (api Go code + docs updates). No UI work is in scope for this item — the admin viewer is execute/lpbs-admin-payment-ops. acceptance_deny is intentionally left empty: there are no secret/generated paths inside the allow globs that need extra protection.

items.topic: Coexistence with the existing intro_anomaly_log table
items.context: The codebase already has intro_anomaly_log + a logIntroAnomaly() writer. The new payment_anomaly_log generalizes the pattern. We need to decide what happens to the old table and its writer when the new one ships. This affects whether any historical reports/queries against intro_anomaly_log keep working.

options.label: Replace logIntroAnomaly's body to forward to LogPaymentAnomaly. Stop writing to intro_anomaly_log entirely. Leave the table in place as a frozen historical record (no migration of past rows).
options.rationale: Cleanest greenfield outcome. One write path, one source of truth going forward. Past rows remain queryable for historical reports; new rows live in payment_anomaly_log only. Aligns with the user's 'no compat shims' preference.

options.label: Dual-write: logIntroAnomaly forwards to LogPaymentAnomaly AND continues to insert into intro_anomaly_log for any anomaly_type starting with 'intro_'.
options.rationale: Preserves any internal dashboards/reports that read intro_anomaly_log without modification. Costs an extra write per intro anomaly and creates two-row drift if one insert fails.

options.label: Migrate: copy all intro_anomaly_log rows into payment_anomaly_log on first boot, then drop intro_anomaly_log.
options.rationale: Single source of truth including historical data. Adds a one-shot migration with rollback considerations and risks data loss if the column mapping is wrong.

items.topic: Webhook payload format — generic JSON vs. Slack/Discord-shaped
items.context: Slack incoming webhooks and Discord webhooks accept POSTs but expect specific JSON shapes (e.g., Slack wants {text, blocks}, Discord wants {content, embeds}). A generic JSON payload is the most portable but won't render nicely in Slack/Discord without an adapter on the receiving end. This affects how operators consume alerts day-one.

options.label: Generic JSON only — single canonical payload (id, type, severity, email, customer_id, subject, details, created_at, scenario). Operators wire up an intermediate forwarder if they want Slack/Discord rendering.
options.rationale: Maximally portable, single code path, easy to test. Matches the 'configurable monitoring endpoint' framing from research d2=B. Integrators (Slack/Discord) handle their own rendering — common pattern with pipedream/n8n/zapier.

options.label: Format adapter — admin selects format = generic | slack | discord; dispatcher renders accordingly. Default generic.
options.rationale: Best day-one operator experience for the common Slack/Discord case. Adds an enum config field, three render paths, and three sets of payload tests.

options.label: Slack-shaped by default — emit Slack-compatible JSON ({text, blocks}). Works directly with Slack incoming webhooks; non-Slack consumers parse as JSON.
options.rationale: Optimizes for the most likely consumer (Slack) but ties the canonical payload shape to a vendor.

items.context: The plan uses an in-process token bucket per anomaly_type. Defaults need to balance noise suppression against missing real incidents. Once the reconciliation ticker and fulfillment tracker start emitting, a too-permissive default causes alert storms; too-strict hides real events. There is no production volume baseline (research listed this as a Limitation).

options.label: Conservative: burst=5, refill=1 token / 60s (max ~1 alert/min/type after burst). Per-type overrides stored in payment_settings.anomaly_rate_limits JSONB.
options.rationale: Safe default: an operator notices the first alert immediately and won't be flooded. The first 5 of any type land instantly so a real incident is not throttled. Per-type overrides give operators an escape hatch.

options.label: Aggressive: burst=20, refill=1/30s. Catches more real-time events at the cost of larger alert volume during incidents.
options.rationale: Better for high-traffic deployments where many distinct events of the same type are normal. Wrong default for the current single-customer-class LPBS deployment.

options.label: Strict: burst=1, refill=1 token / 5min. One alert every 5 minutes per type maximum.
options.rationale: Maximally suppresses storms but risks missing the second real incident of the same type within 5 minutes. Probably too strict for a guardrail surface.

items.context: The webhook URL embeds an authentication token (e.g., a Slack incoming webhook URL is a bearer secret in the path). The plan treats it as a secret: redacted on GET, available via the existing reveal endpoint. Alternative: treat it as a non-secret config field shown plainly in the admin UI.

options.label: Treat as a secret — extend handleRevealStripeSecret's allowed fields to include 'anomaly_webhook_url'. Admin GET shows '<set>' marker; reveal returns plaintext.
options.rationale: Slack/Discord webhook URLs are bearer credentials; anyone with the URL can post into the channel. Matches existing handling for stripe webhook_secret. Consistent UX pattern.

options.label: Treat as plain config — show URL plaintext in the admin GET response.
options.rationale: Simpler — no reveal endpoint change, easier copy/paste UX. Acceptable risk if admin-only access is sufficient protection. Mismatched with stripe webhook_secret handling, which sets a precedent.

items.topic: Where the dispatcher fires — synchronous on insert vs. background sweep
items.context: The plan dispatches on a goroutine fired from inside Log() right after the row is inserted. An alternative is to insert with dispatch_status='pending' and have a separate background sweeper poll for pending rows. This affects latency, simplicity, and behavior on API restart.

options.label: Fire-and-forget at insert time — Log() inserts row, then spawns a goroutine to dispatch. No sweeper.
options.rationale: Simplest. Lowest latency. Failure mode: an alert is lost if the API process crashes between insert and dispatch (rare and acceptable for guardrail alerts — the row stays as evidence).

options.label: Background sweeper — Log() only inserts. A separate goroutine wakes every N seconds, claims rows where dispatch_status='pending', and dispatches them.
options.rationale: Survives crashes (unsent rows get retried on restart). Adds a second concurrent path (lock contention, claim semantics) and ~N seconds of dispatch latency. Sustains a longer outage of the webhook target since rows queue instead of going straight to 'failed'.

options.label: Hybrid — fire-and-forget normally; on startup, sweep for any rows still 'pending' from a prior crash and dispatch them.
options.rationale: Catches the crash case without the steady-state latency of B. Adds boot-time complexity and a one-time sweep query.

plan_updates: Created plan.md scaffold (round 1). All 13 mandatory sections populated using the research conclusion + a code-level audit of existing payment_settings + intro_anomaly_log + stripe_webhook_service + test_helpers. Concrete schema, Go struct, JSON payload shape, retry policy, and 13-test verification matrix in §8-§9. Greenfield constraint and 'no scenario restart' constraints made explicit. Five open decisions in this round target: coexistence with intro_anomaly_log (d1), payload format (d2), rate-limit defaults (d3), URL secret handling (d4), and dispatch model (d5). All other research-level decisions (scheduling=ticker, delivery=webhook) are already settled and baked in.
